record.question: Which of the following insulin analogue has the longest mechanism of action?
record.explanation: Answer A: Insulin glargine. Among the listed analogues, insulin glargine is long acting; lispro, glulisine, and aspart are rapid acting. Source/context note: Newer basal analogues such as degludec may have longer duration but are absent from options. Reference: https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/diabetes/overview/insulin-medicines-treatments. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
